turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on a, an and the?
turns.tutor:
Hello! Let me show you my thinking with one example.
She eats an apple. Before I choose, I say the noun aloud in my head: "apple". It starts with a vowel sound, so I pick an.
One-sentence rule: an comes before a vowel sound, and a comes before other sounds.
Right: I have a pen. Wrong: I have an pen.

Now you try. Write just the missing word:
Write a or an: She has ___ orange in her bag. (answer with only the missing word)
turns.judgeInput:

W2 (wrong) strength 1: a and an are the same; "a" (or "the") goes everywhere. Its error: uses "a" where "an" is needed ("a apple").
C1 (correct) strength 1: a singular countable noun needs a/an (or the). Independent correct productions so far: 0.
C2 (correct) strength 0: an before a vowel sound, a before a consonant sound. Independent correct productions so far: 0.
